sections.title: Data Flow Schema: How VenvHub Provisions VS Code
sections.content:
VenvHub Pro is far more than a simple IDE launcher. It includes deep orchestration logic (within vs_code_json.py and system_sync.py) that actively provisions Visual Studio Code with the exact runtimes, module search paths, and developer tooling required.

sections.title: Safe Non-Destructive Merging in settings.json
sections.content:
VenvHub Pro never destructively overwrites workspace configuration files. It operates using key-level reconciliation:

  • Parse & Preserve: Reads existing settings and preserves personal formatting preferences, linters, and third-party plugin configurations.
  • Interpreter Binding: Purges legacy keys and maps python.defaultInterpreterPath directly to the active python.exe.
  • Fail-Safe Recovery: If settings.json contains syntax errors from manual edits, VenvHub recovers the schema to prevent IntelliSense failure.
  • Clean Teardown: Deleting a default environment cleans obsolete paths. If no configurations remain, removes empty .vscode/ directories automatically.
USB Portability Recovery: When launching from external USB drives on a new PC, VenvHub Pro updates shifted drive letters inside settings.json automatically in milliseconds.

sections.title: Feeding Pylance & IntelliSense Code Analysis
sections.content:
To eliminate false-positive ModuleNotFoundError warnings in the editor, VenvHub provisions Pylance based on module type:

Module TypeIDE Provisioning Method
Local Packages (Linker)Injects absolute directory paths into python.analysis.extraPaths in settings.json. Unlinking cleanly strips paths without touching manual user paths.
Editable Packages (pip -e)No modifications to settings.json required. Pip builds .pth records in site-packages which Pylance discovers natively.

sections.title: Meta-Sync: Injecting Workspace Tasks & Keybindings
sections.content:
When linking local packages containing a local_meta.json descriptor, VenvHub Pro automates workspace provisioning:

  1. Inspects descriptor for "vscode_integration" definitions.
  2. Maps Tasks directly into .vscode/tasks.json.
  3. Maps Keybindings into .vscode/keybindings.json.
  4. Anti-Duplication: Validates existing workspace task labels to prevent duplicate entries across relinking cycles.
Variable Expansion: Tasks bind dynamically to ${command:python.interpreterPath}, guaranteeing they execute inside the active default Venv.
